finding: NHS England pilot (Dec 2024-Apr 2025): lab arm at Doncaster, St George's and Exeter; POC arm at Salford. 88% of lab-arm patients needing a clopidogrel prescription had been discharged before results; 100% of POC-arm patients had results on the ward. Non-responders 33% (POC) vs 29% (lab). POC failure rate 0.49%.
source: Genedrive pilot-results release (genedrive.com), PHG Foundation blog
reliability: Medium: company-reported, pooled across three lab sites, not site-specific
used_for: Timing evidence Possible and readiness Medium for S007, S049, S065; supports the national time-sensitivity case

finding: Genedrive trading update 13 Jul 2026: Salford routine use; North Bristol (Southmead) implementation under way; North West Anglia (Peterborough) use established; about 15 sites in total (UK and international); about 85% of patients discharged before lab results in NHS England logistics pilots. The "approximately 25 business cases" in that release relates to MT-RNR1, NOT CYP2C19.
used_for: Corrects an earlier assumption in this project that 25 CYP2C19 business cases exist. Do not quote it.

finding: Peterborough City Hospital Acute Stroke Centre adopted the Genedrive kit (announcement dated about Mar 2025); trust identified as North West Anglia NHS FT in the Jul 2026 update.
used_for: S014 status set to Routine use (Genedrive incumbent), so excluded from the greenfield ranking. Status text taken from the Jul 2026 update, which says use is established.

finding: East Genomics implementation guidance v0.3.5 (Dec 2025): CYP2C19 for stroke is not yet approved for routine commissioning; the NHS Genomic Medicine Service does not commission point-of-care tests; POC costs fall to the trust. No sample-to-result turnaround is stated for any route.
source: East Genomics / Cambridge University Hospitals guidance PDF
used_for: Implementation readiness context: the funding route is the trust, for lab or POC alike. Turnaround must come from each lab (not published).

finding: NHS Tayside (Scotland) lab-based service: 2,300 patients tested Apr 2022-Mar 2024; 29% poor/intermediate metabolisers; 98.9% of results back within one week. Ward pharmacist champion; IT integration was a barrier.
used_for: Benchmark for a well-run lab pathway (about one week). Context only, not scored.

finding: Salford HASU: 586 patients tested in the first seven months; about one third non-responders; result in about one hour; machines in ED and HASU; results on ward before discharge.
used_for: Reference case for POC-led pathway design

finding: Doncaster and Bassetlaw (DBTH) tested 130 stroke patients Dec 2024-Apr 2025; 20% had a reduced-response variant (lower than 29-33% elsewhere). Test type and turnaround not stated.
used_for: Supports the Doncaster pilot-site flag. The 20% is a possible local variation in loss-of-function rate to test later.

finding: No site-specific evidence of CYP2C19 testing route, turnaround or business case found for these shortlisted sites: Northwick Park, York, Royal Stoke, Coventry, Sheffield, Charing Cross, Dorset, Aintree, East Kent, UCLH, QE Birmingham, Southampton, Newcastle RVI, New Cross, Eastbourne, Whiston, North Durham, Gloucestershire, Leicester, Hull, Stepping Hill, Lincoln, Northumbria, Hampshire, Cumberland, Ipswich, Romford, Derby. Searches returned only generic literature. These remain Unknown (neutral), not low.
source: Web searches by site name and trust (Oct 2026)
used_for: Left unchanged. Needs ICB/trust contact or FOI-style requests, which is what outreach is for.

finding: Royal Berkshire NHS FT publishes a patient leaflet "CYP2C19 genetic testing following a stroke or TIA" (Feb 2026), so a testing service exists there. The leaflet PDF could not be opened, so POC vs lab and turnaround are unknown. Royal Berkshire is outside the 30-site shortlist.
used_for: Readiness Medium for S058; candidate for the evidence pass or outreach

finding: Not read: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06292117 (implementation of onsite rapid CYP2C19 assay) could not be fetched (permission not granted); NCT06943586 returned no content. Site lists in these records could identify further trial or pilot sites.

The "586 patients" in the ESOC 2026 abstract (HASU, 0.17% failure, 64-76 minutes, 32.5% non-responders) matches the HSJ figure for Salford (586 patients, first seven months). Same patient count and setting, so very likely the same cohort. Attribution is inferred from the matching count, not stated in the abstract.
used_for: Used as the Salford volume benchmark in 13_CALIBRATION

finding: Genedrive's pilot release names the four national pilot sites as Doncaster, St George's and Exeter (lab) and Salford (POC). East Kent is not among them, which answers the validation question "was East Kent a pilot site?". East Kent clinicians (D. Hargroves) are nonetheless poster authors on the pilot results and in the CERSI-PGx guideline affiliations, so the site is close to the evidence without having been a pilot site.
source: Genedrive pilot-results release; UK Stroke Forum poster list; validation E16-E17
used_for: East Kent case: champion present, no pilot, route unknown
